fixes.explanation: Good guess on the building, friend. Paul was in the synagogue, but Acts 18:19 says he went in and reasoned with the Jews. That's the thing he does there. The text says nothing about him praying alone.

I see why you'd say that, baker. They asked him to stay. But Acts 18:20 says that when they asked him to stay for a while longer, he declined. So the answer is False. He said no, and the very next verse gives them a promise.
Yes, baker. Acts 18:22 says that after landing at Caesarea, Paul went up and greeted the church at Jerusalem. Then he went down to Antioch. Up to Jerusalem, then down to Antioch.

Corinth is where Paul had stayed for quite some time, friend (Acts 18:18). But this verse follows the trip from Ephesus, where he set sail (Acts 18:21). After landing at Caesarea, he greets the church at Jerusalem (Acts 18:22).

Peter is a famous name, so I see the pull, friend. But Acts 18:25 says Apollos knew only the baptism of John. The verse still calls him instructed in the way of the Lord and fervent in spirit. So he had plenty going for him, with that one gap.

Philip is a name you might remember, but he isn't in this verse, friend. Acts 18:25 says Apollos knew only the baptism of John. That's the one gap the verse names. The same verse says he spoke and taught accurately about Jesus.

Ouch, friend. Picture someone fixing you in front of a whole crowd. That's not what the text says happened. Acts 18:26 says that when Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him aside and explained to him the way of God more accurately. They explained, and they didn't make a show of it.

Nothing in the text says they told him to stop, friend. Acts 18:26 says they took him aside and explained to him the way of God more accurately. They taught him more. Paul isn't mentioned in that verse.

I get why you'd think so, since friends can be nervous about a goodbye. But Acts 18:27 says the brothers encouraged him and wrote to the disciples there to welcome him. So the answer is False. They cheered him on and wrote a letter for him.
Right, baker. Acts 18:27 says the brothers encouraged him and wrote to the disciples in Achaia to welcome him. They didn't hold him back. They backed him up with a letter.

Signs and wonders happen in Acts, like in Acts 2:43, so it's an easy one to pick. But not here. Acts 18:28 says he was proving from the Scriptures that Jesus is the Christ. The Scriptures are the tool this verse names.
